rules: Celebrity/politician-launched coins with presale, gifted or team-held supply dump within hours; the first candle is the top.
If one wallet, cluster or multisig holds >50% of supply (check Bubblemaps), assume it is the exit for insiders.
Fresh wallets funded on launch day among top holders = sniper/insider setup; avoid.
Serial launch operators (Hayden Davis/Kelsier, Sahil Arora) repeat the same rug playbook: check who is behind the launch.
A famous name alone is not a meme; coins need a funny/cute shareable character or moment.
When the real person or meme source posts one contract, only that contract matters; all copies die.
Among copies, the winner is usually the earliest coin with the exact name and exact ticker that graduates the bonding curve fast.
First is not enough: fairer supply, active CTO community and more liquidity beat the first-launched version (NEIRO ETH beat SOL).
Tier-1 CEX listing (Binance/Coinbase) picks the final winner among copies; the oldest exact-name, highest-volume coin gets listed.
When an existing coin already has the exact name, a big viral post sends flow to it, not to new launches (PENGUIN, KEKIUS, LABUBU).
A specific named object/character inside a mega-brand beats generic brand coins (Dacity Coin vs generic GTA 6 coins).
Being positioned before the reveal (leaks, rumors) wins; launching after the news means fighting dozens of copies.
Variants ('wif hat', 'baby', 'girl', 'not a') stay small; split tickers cap the upside of even huge memes.
Cute, funny, alive viral animals run big (MOODENG, PNUT); sad news, deaths and serious events give short, small pumps.
Coins tied to a celebrity's temporary choice (X name, pfp) crash the moment they change it.
'Rival' or rumor coins ('X will launch a coin', DADDY vs MOTHER) are borrowed hype and die with the trend.
Viral-animal and trend coins peak within ~1-3 weeks; treat them as trades, not holds.
Dev/influencer selling, rugging or stunts kill trust instantly; dev behaviour after launch decides survival.
Real charity donations and launchpad/official-account reposts help pick 'the one' among copies but don't create the run alone.

cases.name: Hawk Tuah girl coin
cases.meme: Haliey Welch, the viral 'Hawk Tuah' street-interview girl, launched her own token.
cases.lesson: Celebrity launch + presale/gifted supply to insiders = instant dump; never chase the first candle.

cases.name: LIBRA (Milei)
cases.meme: Argentina's president Javier Milei posted a token supposedly to fund Argentine businesses.
cases.lesson: Politician/official-looking coins run by launch 'facilitators' with most supply unlocked are exit liquidity traps.

cases.name: MELANIA (official)
cases.meme: Official Melania Trump coin launched one day after TRUMP, before the inauguration.
cases.lesson: The second coin of the same celebrity/family is a dilution, not a new winner; team-controlled supply bleeds out.

cases.name: Caitlyn Jenner coin
cases.meme: Caitlyn Jenner launched her own celebrity token during the mid-2024 celeb-coin wave.
cases.lesson: A famous name is not a meme; promoter-run celebrity coins have no organic buyers after launch day.

cases.name: Jason Derulo coin
cases.meme: Singer Jason Derulo promoted his own token.
cases.lesson: If one promoter cluster holds a big chunk of supply, the coin is their exit, not yours.

cases.name: Iggy Azalea coin
cases.meme: Rapper Iggy Azalea's 'mother' token, the most successful of the 2024 celeb coins.
cases.lesson: Even the best celebrity coin fades once the celeb stops posting; the peak is in the first weeks.

cases.name: Andrew Tate coin
cases.meme: Andrew Tate promoted 'DADDY' as a rival to Iggy's MOTHER.
cases.lesson: A 'rival' coin made to flip another celeb coin has borrowed hype and dies with the trend.

cases.name: Kanye West coin
cases.meme: Kanye West (Ye) launched YZY as an 'official' token tied to his brand.
cases.lesson: If one wallet/multisig holds most supply and snipers own the first block, the celebrity is the marketing for insiders.

cases.name: Central African Republic coin
cases.meme: The president of the Central African Republic announced a national meme coin.
cases.lesson: 'Nation/official' coins with <10% public float are not memes, they are insider distributions.

cases.name: Wolf of Wall Street coin
cases.meme: Token riding rumors that Jordan Belfort (the real Wolf of Wall Street) would launch a coin.
cases.lesson: Coins based on a rumor that a famous person 'will launch' are usually set up by insiders to sell the rumor.

cases.name: Dave Portnoy coins
cases.meme: Barstool's Dave Portnoy promoted a 'Stool Prisondente' token and launched/sold GREED.
cases.lesson: Influencer-promoted coins live and die by that one wallet; if the influencer sells once, it is over.

cases.name: Hunter Biden LAPTOP coin
cases.meme: Hunter Biden launched a coin named after his infamous laptop.
cases.lesson: Thin-liquidity launches by famous people get sniped and dumped in the first hour; top holders that are fresh wallets = red flag.

cases.name: Gen Z Quant kid rug
cases.meme: A teen livestreamed rugging his own Pump.fun coin and flipping off chat.
cases.lesson: Revenge/story pumps are one-day events; ride early or skip, never hold.

cases.name: Pope coins (Francis death / Leo XIV election)
cases.meme: Coins launched on Pope Francis's death and Pope Leo XIV's election.
cases.lesson: Big serious news (deaths, elections, religion) gives one-day pumps; it is not a lasting meme character.

cases.name: Musk 'Harry Bolz' name coins
cases.meme: Coins named after Elon Musk's temporary X display name 'Harry Bolz'.
cases.lesson: Coins that depend on a celebrity keeping a profile name/pfp die the moment they change it.

cases.name: GTA 6 coin flood (Jan 2025)
cases.meme: Generic GTA 6 hype coins before any official trailer content.
cases.lesson: Generic 'big brand' coins with no specific moment or object split into dozens and all die.

cases.name: TRUMP vs copycats
cases.meme: Donald Trump launched an official coin days before his inauguration.
cases.lesson: When the real person posts a contract, only that contract matters; every copy is a scam within minutes.

cases.name: Moo Deng vs copies
cases.meme: Baby pygmy hippo at Thailand's Khao Kheow zoo going viral.
cases.lesson: For viral animals: the earliest coin with the exact animal name and ticker that graduates fast becomes 'the one'.

cases.name: Peanut the Squirrel vs copies
cases.meme: Pet squirrel Peanut seized and euthanized by NY officials; became a US election talking point.
cases.lesson: A CEX listing (Binance/Coinbase) picks the winner among copies; the coin most likely to list is the oldest exact-name one with most volume.

cases.name: Chill Guy vs copies
cases.meme: 'Just a chill guy' cartoon dog trend on TikTok.
cases.lesson: Exact trend name + ticker, launched as the trend rises, beats every variant ('wif hat', 'girl', 'not a').

cases.name: CZ's dog Broccoli vs copies
cases.meme: CZ revealed his dog's name is Broccoli.
cases.lesson: For crypto-figure memes, the coin on that figure's home chain with the exact name wins; front-run guesses die.

cases.name: Neiro (Kabosu's successor) ETH vs SOL
cases.meme: Neiro, the new dog adopted by the Doge (Kabosu) owner.
cases.lesson: First isn't enough: the version with the fairest supply and a strong CTO community attracts the CEX listing and wins.

cases.name: GOAT (Truth Terminal) vs fakes
cases.meme: AI bot Truth Terminal preaching the 'Goatse gospel'; anon made a coin and the AI endorsed it.
cases.lesson: If the meme's source account endorses one contract, that one wins; copies lack the voice that keeps the story alive.

cases.name: Kekius Maximus vs copies
cases.meme: Elon Musk changed his X name to 'Kekius Maximus' with a Pepe-gladiator pfp.
cases.lesson: Pre-existing exact-name coin wins the copy war, but if the meme depends on a celeb's temporary choice, sell into the pump.

cases.name: Labubu vs name clones
cases.meme: Pop Mart's Labubu toy craze.
cases.lesson: When an old brand/character re-trends, the oldest exact-name coin with history wins the revival.

cases.name: Tung Tung Tung Sahur (Italian brainrot) coins
cases.meme: Italian brainrot AI character Tung Tung Tung Sahur.
cases.lesson: A huge kids/TikTok meme does not guarantee a big coin; split tickers cap the upside.

cases.name: Nietzschean Penguin + White House post
cases.meme: White House posted Trump walking hand in hand with a penguin; links to the 'nihilist penguin' meme.
cases.lesson: When a big account posts a meme, buyers pile into the existing coin with that exact name, not new launches.

cases.name: Punch the baby monkey
cases.meme: Rejected baby macaque at Ichikawa City Zoo, Japan, who bonded with a plush orangutan.
cases.lesson: Cute-animal coins peak within ~2-3 weeks of the story; plan exits, don't treat as a long hold.

cases.name: Dacity Coin (GTA 6 trailer) vs other Dacity tokens
cases.meme: Fictional 'Dacity Coin' crypto shown for ~2 seconds in the GTA 6 launch trailer (AudaCity brand).
cases.lesson: A specific named object inside a mega-brand beats generic brand coins; being positioned before the reveal wins.

cases.name: Fiona the hippo coins (Nov 2026)
cases.meme: Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo, died Nov 19, 2026 after swallowing a hat.
cases.lesson: Death/sad-news animal coins stay small; donations help pick 'the one' but don't create a Moo Deng-size run.

cases.name: Jimothy the Raccoon
cases.meme: Real short-spined raccoon filmed near a Seattle Goodwill.
cases.lesson: Launchpad/official-account reposts concentrate flow into one coin among copies.
